# Introduction

The assortment of beer products in the US market is vast and consists of more than 500 different beer products including non-alcoholic beer in our dataset. The choices an american consumer has to decide which beer can quite literally be very overwhelming. The question is then, how strongly do consumers substitute between different beer segments, and can the Rotterdam and AIDS model lead to different conclusions about price sensitivity and competition?

To try to find answers to these questions, we will use the Dominick's dataset which contains weekly data on beer sales in the Chicago area. Our analysis will focus on the demand for beer products in the US market, and we will estimate both the Rotterdam and AIDS models to compare their results. We will also discuss the implications of our findings for the beer industry and policy. Since the dataset also contains data on non-alcoholic beer, we will also look at the demand for non-alcoholic beer and how it compares to the demand for alcoholic beer.

In the next section we will present a literature review of relevant studies on the same or similar products/commodities. We will then present our theoretical framework, data section, methods, estimated results, and discussion and implications.

## Literature review

### The german whitefish market

@bronnmann2016german uses the Almost Ideal Demand System (AIDS) to estimate the demand for whitefish in Germany. They find that the demand for whitefish is  relatively price elastic, and that there is a significant substitution effect between different types of whitefish. They did not estimate a Rotterdam model, however we will be building upon their work by estimating the AIDS model and also the Rotterdam model to compare the results.

### Meat demand in the UK

In United Kingdom, @fousekis2000meat estimates the demand for meat using both the Rotterdam and AIDS model. They find that the Rotterdam model better explain consumers retail purchasing behavior with fixed price effects, compared to the AIDS model with variable price effects. They also found that the real expenditure and the Hicksian demand elasticities are found to be different than earlier studies using AIDS models. 

### The Silence of the lambdas

@alston1993silence tests both the AIDS and Rotterdam models on the demand for U.S meat products. In conclusion they find that the Almost Ideal System model is rejected, while the Rotterdam model is not. They also state in the paper that the Rotterdam model is seeing renewed interest in demand for alcoholic beverages.

### Competition of beverage products in the current market

@heng2018competition is a similar study to ours, but they look at the competition between beverage products in the current market. Their findings indicate that consumers substitute refrigerated juice with low calorie drinks, and that a larger prooprtion of consumers substitute soft drinks with fruit drinks.

# Brief theory framework


## The Rotterdam Model

The Rotterdam model was introduced in @theil1965analysis and is based on the idea that consumers have a utility function that is linear in the logarithm of prices and quantities. The model can be estimated using a system of equations, and allows for the estimation of both own-price and cross-price elasticities. The Rotterdam model is a flexible functional form that can accommodate a wide range of demand systems, and has been widely used in empirical studies of consumer demand.

## An Almost Ideal Demand System

The AIDS model is a newer approach to estimating demand systems, and was proposed in @deaton1980almost. The model is based on the idea that consumers have a utility function that is linear in the logarithm of prices and quantities, and that the demand for each good is a function of the prices of all goods and the total expenditure on all goods. The model can be estimated using a system of equations, and allows for the estimation of both own-price and cross-price elasticities.

\section{Appendix General AI Use}

When we write code in Visual Studio Code or RStudio, we use a plugin called GitHub Copilot. This plugin will try to suggest code or sentences(even paragraphs) as we are writing. We sometimes accept the suggestions but only if it's how we would do it. There are also cases where it can be seen in the code that we comment with a "plotting year on x, value on y" so that it will just autofill the code we usually use.

Documenting each of these instances would be cumbersome and wouldn't serve any purpose. All code sections with such comments can be assumed to have involved GitHub Copilot. More information about this AI tool is available at <https://github.com/features/copilot>.
